subject: Game Theory
title: Endorsement Games
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Endorsement Games.

hook.text: When a party leader endorses a candidate early, it signals electability—and discourages other contenders.

buildup.text: Endorsements are strategic signals: they transfer credibility and coordinate supporters around one candidate.

discovery.text: Early endorsements compress primaries. Late endorsements allow leaders to back the likely winner safely.

twist.text: Endorsing the wrong candidate is costly. Leaders risk reputation, so they wait for clearer signals.

climax.text: The 'invisible primary'—the endorsement race before votes are cast—often predicts the eventual nominee.

quiz.question: Why do party leaders sometimes delay endorsements?
options: Endorsing a loser is costly to their reputation
